newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan assembly backs death penalty for gang-rape.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan assembly backs death penalty for gang-rape.

text.p: Pakistan's National Assemebly (lower house of parliament) passed a bill on Wednesday prescribing the death penalty for gang-rape, carrying out a pledge made by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
To become law, the bill must also be passed by the Senate (upper house), where Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party and its allies are in an overwhelming majority.

PML parliamentary secretary for law Zafar Ali Shah told the house the bill amended an Islamic law enforced by military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq in 1979 that provided for prison terms of four to 25 years and 30 lashes for such an offence.
"For sometime past, there has been a tendency towards gang-rapes so that there was a need for creating a deterrence against such a heinous offence by prescribing the death penalty," he said.

"Now when zina bil-jabr (forcible sexual intercourse) liable to tazir (punishment) is committed by two or more persons in furtherance of a common intention of all, each of such persons shall be punished with death," he said.
Sharif had promised to bring such a law in a broadcast when he took office in February after his party's landslide victory in elections the same month.

No figures were immediately available on the incidence of gang rapes in Pakistan. But local newspapers have often reported such incidents, mostly in rural areas of the central province of Punjab, sometimes for settling family feuds.
